ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First look at the image: in the picture there are five rows of clues, respectively 4132, 9826, 5079, 2741, 7642, corresponding to the textual explanations shown in the picture. The reasoning is as follows: from 7642 it is known that 7, 6, 4, and 2 are all not in the four-digit number. Thus in 4132, only 1 and 3 can be correct, and both are in the wrong positions, so 1 and 3 are both in the answer, 1 is not in the 2nd position, and 3 is not in the 3rd position. Looking again at 2741, because 2, 7, and 4 have already been eliminated, only 1 may be correct; and it is also in the wrong position, so 1 is not in the 4th position. From this, 1 is neither in the 2nd position nor in the 4th position. Look at 9826: 2 and 6 have already been eliminated, so the one that is correct and in the correct position can only be 9 in the 1st position or 8 in the 2nd position. Looking again at 5079: 7 has already been eliminated, so exactly two digits among them are correct, and one is in the correct position and one is in the wrong position. If 8 is in the 2nd position, then 9 is not in the number, and the correct ones in 5079 can only be 5 and 0, which together with the previously determined 1, 3, and 8 would exceed the digit-limit of the four-digit number, so it does not hold; therefore 9 must be in the 1st position. In this way, the other correct digit in 5079 can only be 0, and 0 in the 2nd position is in the correct position, while 9 in that row is in the wrong position. The remaining 1 and 3 are placed respectively in the 3rd position and the 4th position; and because 1 cannot be in the 2nd position or the 4th position, it can only be in the 3rd position, therefore 3 is in the 4th position. The last digit is 3.
